newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus tells Soros Fund to pay $3 mln taxes.
newsitem.headline: Belarus tells Soros Fund to pay $3 mln taxes.

text.p: Belarus authorities have slapped a $3 million tax demand on the Soros Fund -- despite previous assurances it would have tax-exempt status, the organisation said on Wednesday.

"We were accused of various violations and of making profits," the Belarussian branch of the organisation, set up by philanthropic tycoon George Soros to help post-Communist societies, said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
It said it had also been told to pay the equivalent of almost $3 million in tax, despite the fact that it was awarded tax-free status in 1995.
Relations between the Fund and the Belarussian authorities have worsened since March when Minsk barred its local executive, Peter Byrne, from entering the country.
He was accused of sponsoring the opposition, including members of the mass media who criticise President Alexander Lukashenko's authoritarian style of rule.
The Fund said $3 million represented half of its spending in Belarus last year. Over four years the Fund has donated $13 million to educational, ecological and cultural programmes.

Washington criticised Minsk for barring Byrne, and relations with the United States have grown increasingly bad, especially after a U.S. diplomat was expelled and Ambassador Kenneth Yalowitz was recalled to Washington for consultations on March 25.
But Yalowitz returned to Minsk on Wednesday, bringing what the embassy said was a tough message about the government's "abysmal human rights record".
Washington is Lukashenko's loudest critic, slamming him in particular for his crackdowns on political opposition.
State Department spokesman Nicolas Burns said on Tuesday that Washington was "determined to send a signal of our strong support for democracy and strong opposition to dictatorship".
In March, Washington cut off $40 million in aid because of Minsk's human rights record.
